reasons: The cited Section 13 contains a Vendor-side (Garman) indemnity in the Customer's (Sparkling's) favour covering all Losses including settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees, backed by an ownership/non-encumbrance warranty and the standard infringement remedy ladder (procure rights, substitute equivalent element, replace/modify) — which satisfies the rule's fallback position of a Vendor IP indemnity with usual remedies.

No one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services exists anywhere in the cited text, so the walk-away scenario does not apply; Section 15 also carves Section 13 breaches out of the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion, which is more favourable than the fallback's 3x super-cap.

Per the playbook's classification semantics, a clause meeting the fallback is compliant and is not redlined; the rationale correctly records the shortfalls versus the preferred position (no express 'defend'/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund remedy, no breach-of-law/data-breach/gross-negligence limbs, affiliates unnamed, tight ten-day notice) as sub-elements rather than fallback failures.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: the indemnity is triggered by breach of the ownership/no-encumbrance warranty and the same paragraph expressly addresses the consequences where the Work 'is held to constitute an infringement of another Person's rights', so an IP indemnity is in substance present.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is proposed; the finding is properly retained as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue.
